submissionAttempts.body:
The applicable ordering guarantee is the GLOBAL total order (Record A: one shared position space over committed state revisions), not the per-consumer formulation (Record B).

Integration: this workspace is Palimpsest, whose external side effects run through the sibling project Ordarium on the shared local operations ledger (src/effects/runtime.ts builds the pinned SqliteLedger). The conflicting sources are two Palimpsest-local interface records, docs/engineering/09-ordering-contract-a.md (global) and 09-ordering-contract-b.md (per-consumer); both are stamped "normative, current scope", so their own labels are circular and cannot decide the question. The tie-break comes from the pinned Ordarium contract this workspace actually consumes.

Decisive evidence (pinned ordarium-v1.3.1, per package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides):
- @ordarium/core types.d.ts: state changes are delivered in "durable ledger commit-observation order, ascending (ORD-BOOT-0)"; StateChangePage.cursor is an "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change".
- @ordarium/ledger-sqlite index.js changes(): "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; pages with ORDER BY c.change_seq ASC and validates the cursor against the whole-ledger high-water mark SELECT MAX(change_seq).
- migrations.js: ordarium_state_changes(change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, ...) is a single global sequence; the v3->v4 migration doc says "v3 recorded no global commit order... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order". Capability stateChangeFeed: true.

Reading: the ordering axis is one global, durable, filter-independent sequence shared by every consumer. A consumer does keep its own cursor value (resume bookkeeping), but that value is a position in the single shared order; namespace filtering only omits entries, it never creates a per-consumer or per-namespace order. Record B is therefore true only in the trivial cursor-storage sense and false as an ordering guarantee, so it is not what applies.

Provenance/authority: docs/engineering/00-heritage.md §2/§5 and 07-ordarium-alignment.md §0-1 place ledger/effect-layer contract authority with Ordarium (its docs/12-17), with Palimpsest referencing it rather than owning it. The pinned 1.3.1 release artifacts are the frozen embodiment of the "current pinned line" both records claim to describe; Record A is consistent with them, Record B is contradicted by them. The question is resolvable locally from the pinned artifact, so no peer consultation was required.

Caveat: Palimpsest src/ currently has no call sites for StateChangeFeed/changes(), so this is a forward interface record rather than an exercised path; but the guarantee governing the pinned integration remains the global one.

RESOLVED: Record A applies. The state-change feed ordering guarantee at the pinned ordarium-v1.3.1 line is GLOBAL — one ledger-wide position space (ordarium_state_changes.change_seq) shared by all readers.

The peer owning the contract (ordarium.main, owner of ORD-BOOT-0/0.1) confirmed this in thread thr_999f1643-39cf-44af-a231-4d7b5093b0ad (event evt_aa502de6-aa12-4cb3-a18d-333fda05fba0, "decision", 2026-09-11), and stated that reply is the accepted authority basis; no BoundaryContract revision is needed.

The true proposition is a conjunction, not a choice between the two records:
- ONE shared global position space — the ordering guarantee (Record A).
- Per-consumer cursor VALUES are host-owned bookkeeping inside that one shared space (the only sense in which Record B holds).
There is no per-consumer sequence, no per-consumer high-water mark, and no per-namespace position space; a filter narrows only the returned set.

Authoritative citations supplied by the owner (highest first):
1. docs/13 §11 (ORDARIUM-ACTION-2): cursor is opaque, global (filter-independent), and still returns a resume position at the end; on 0.1, validation is against the global high-water, not a namespace-local maximum, and cross-filter cursor semantics are unchanged.
2. docs/17 §16.11/§16.12 (ORDARIUM-GOALS-3): ORD-BOOT-0 registered as durable ledger commit-observation order + global cursor; 0.1 hardening registered; "State feed" acceptance row.
3. ORD-BOOT-0 frozen spec §5: global, filter-independent (approach A) — position space is decoupled from the filter, one cursor is reusable across filters and means "skip everything globally at or before this position"; §7: filtering affects only the returned set, not the global position space.
4. ORD-BOOT-0.1 frozen spec §5 ("global / filter-independent cursor — unchanged"); §3-§4: future-cursor validation compares against the whole-ledger high-water.
5. Pinned declaration snapshot: StateChangePage.cursor = "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change".
6. Pinned implementation (@ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 changes()): comment "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; query WHERE c.change_seq > ? [AND namespace = ?] ORDER BY c.change_seq ASC.

Supersession scope (no version split): ORD-BOOT-0.1 supersedes only ORD-BOOT-0 §5 future-cursor behavior and §7 allowed limit domain. The global/filter-independent clause survives and is restated as unchanged (0.1 §5), so the records cannot be reconciled by version scope: Record B is simply not supported by any Ordarium text. Likely provenance of the B misreading (to be corrected on the Palimpsest side): ORD-BOOT-0 §2 non-goal ("consumer cursor ownership stays host") read as "per-consumer positions"; and ORD-BOOT-0 §9 (v3 recorded no global commit order; "from v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order") — a statement about pre-v4 history, not about 1.3.1 semantics.

Caveats carried into Palimpsest:
- "Global" means whole ledger, not across distinct ledger files. LedgerIdentityBinding is DEFER (0.1 §9): a cursor from ledger A is undetectable against ledger B when A's position <= B's high-water, so one fixed coordination DB must be used.
- MemoryLedger is volatile but keeps the same single-position-space ordering semantics per instance (0.1 §8): durability differs, ordering does not.
- Local workspace note: Palimpsest src/ does not yet call StateChangeFeed.changes(), so this is currently a forward interface record; the guarantee for the pinned integration is nonetheless global.

Local artifact evidence (consistent with the owner's ruling): ordarium_state_changes(change_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT); changes() validates cursors against SELECT MAX(change_seq) and pages ORDER BY change_seq ASC; migrateFromV3 documents that v3 had no global commit order and v4+ carries the real durable database order.

finalAnswerPreview: The peer (Ordarium, owner of the contract) has answered authoritatively. Let me acknowledge the batch and then close the item on that basis.
